items.q: probably like Richard Wyands playing piano, and guys like Earl May on bass, these things like that, so it’s a great band.

ctx.x: He actually used to sub in Duke’s band sometimes when Harry wasn’t there. But Haywood told me like the first time he ever did it, you know he went in there and was like what’s going to happen, they’re all like, this could be a drag. And Haywood got on the bandstand and he started playing and someone said in the back, you could hear someone say, “All right everything’s going to be all right. So what was I telling the story about? I’m losing it. Oh, oh, the riff, the riff. So anyway, we used to do a lot of gigs. I…

never try to fool them to think they’re going to get top 40. And there was people who really wanted it. So three of us are up there, horn players, and we’re playing, someone’s taking a solo, we set riffs, so I set a few riffs. And so one time after Haywood heard a few of the riffs I was setting, he always gave me a ride home with his wife Mil. And he said, “Boy you sound real good, man. And you know those colored riffs.”
